findings.reason: the plan states two different orders for two nodes that write one file, so a coordinator following the followup violates §5's own prerequisite and cannot tell which order is intended.
findings.text: §5 was changed to write reckon/crew/review.py and to state it "runs after §4, which also writes review.py", but the followup at :310 orders "§3 and §5 first; §4 after §3", so the driving prompt builds §5 before the prerequisite the section now declares, against a module both nodes edit

findings.reason: the section's primary artefact has no measure at all, so its gate can pass on a rubric that contradicts the parser shipped beside it, and the gap is what §11 (last) would otherwise be forced to catch at runtime.
findings.text: the done-when parses a fixed reviewer output through the parser and never reads reckon/crew/prompts/health_review.md, the section's named deliverable and the artefact §6 composes with, §7 and §9 invoke, and §11 runs; a rubric prompt missing one of the six items, or the one-treatment constraint, still passes the gate

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — parse_plan_review_report resolves at reckon/crew/review.py:742, and reckon/interface_counts.py and reckon/clones.py exist, with counts() returning exactly the four figures §5 names.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §5's gate (line 155) parses a fixed reviewer output through the parser and never reads the section's named deliverable, the rubric prompt at reckon/crew/prompts/health_review.md, so the headline artefact is unmeasured.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate is a committed pytest file (tests/test_health_review_parses.py); no scratchpad or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new names (health_review.md, the six rubric items, the health parser) carry no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the six items and the one-treatment rule are what the parser enforces, the four interface figures are reckon/interface_counts.py's four counted families, and §6 is named as the caller that composes the brief.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 names one deliverable family, the health-review rubric and the parser of its output landing together, closed by one parse gate.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5 now declares it "runs after §4, which also writes review.py" (line 160), but the driving followup seeds §5 into the first wave with §3 while placing §4 only "after §3" (line 310), and the two nodes edit the same module.
